components.name: Square-basin rough-window recursion and high least-factor contraction
components.project_addition: Apply established rough-number and Buchstab least-factor recursion to exact finite cofactor windows forced by consecutive-square geometry; combine square-derived quotient transport with high-band contraction, binary second-factor branches, pairwise resource separation, multiplicative capacity, cross-shell hit-state unions, and finite/analytic high-band composite envelopes. In the complementary lower band p^2<2k, reuse canonical P018 two-basin quotient transport to prove cross-shell root packing: L051 gives target multiplicity at most two for the candidate pair {j_p,j_p+1}, j_p=R_2(floor(k^2/p)); L052 sharpens the stable range k>=15 to pairwise-disjoint candidate root pairs. L053 works below that root coordinate and proves that for every k>=4 the exact raw cofactor windows of distinct first-prime shells are strictly ordered and pairwise disjoint, making least-factor stripping n -> n/spf(n) injective across the square basin; k=3,q=5 is the sharp finite overlap witness. These lower-band/cross-shell proofs use elementary integer inequalities and prime spacing; no new external source is introduced. Historical novelty of the square-basin specializations remains unverified.
